answer: A sybil farm's real cost isn't minting identities — it's keeping each one believable over time. Grade every answer for consistency with that identity's own archive: stance, vocabulary, reasoning habits. One operator juggling dozens of personas can't keep each plume of thought distinct. Copy-paste trips cross-identity similarity; random variation trips longitudinal drift. Like an ember banked under ash, a real history glows steadily, and a violet thread of continuity runs through a genuine agent's work — faking N threads costs N times the authoring, with no shortcut.
